sections.h2: Where do Isabella County deeds get recorded?
sections.html:
Isabella County deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds in Room 220 of 200 N. Main Street, Mount Pleasant, MI 48858. The phone number is (989) 317-4089. The office keeps land records that reach back to the mid-1800s, and once a document is recorded anyone may review or copy it. Staff do not prepare documents or answer legal questions, so the paperwork needs to be finished by an attorney or closing company before it arrives.

Mount Pleasant is the county seat and largest city. The county was described by the territorial legislature in 1831 and organized in 1859, and it was named for Queen Isabella I of Castile. If you are selling a house in Isabella County, the deed signed at your closing is filed here, and the county site recommends reviewing every document against the recording rules before you submit it.

sections.h2: What is the statutory charge to record in Isabella County?
sections.html:
The statutory charge is a flat $30.00 for each document. A document that lists more than one liber and page adds $3.00 for each one past the first, because one is included at no charge. The office asks you to enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want mailed documents returned.

sections.h2: Which sales in Isabella County need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
Under MCL 211.135, a tax certificate from the County Treasurer must be in hand before the Register of Deeds records the following:

  • A warranty deed.
  • Any deed that contains a covenant of warranty.
  • A land contract.
  • An assignment of a land contract with a warranty clause.
  • A master deed for a condominium.

The treasurer, not the Register of Deeds, issues the certificate, and your check for it is made out to the Isabella County Treasurer. A long list of descriptions costs a little more, at 20 cents each after the fifth. Ask your closing agent to request the certificate before the signing date so it does not hold up the filing.

sections.h2: What recording rules do Isabella County deeds have to meet?
sections.html:
The county posts a summary of Michigan's most requested recording requirements and points to the Michigan Legislature website for the full text. The items below come from that list:

  • Signatures are original, with the names typed, stamped or printed beneath them, and names must agree among the body, signature and acknowledgment.
  • The addresses of all parties appear on an instrument that conveys, assigns or encumbers title.
  • A deed signed in Michigan has an acknowledgment by a notary public and shows the drafter's name and address.
  • When a conveyance names a survivor in the grantor's section, a certified death certificate is recorded as its own document.
  • A trust agreement that accompanies an instrument is recorded separately, under Public Act 194 of 2018.
  • Court orders are certified and sealed by the court clerk.
  • Margins are 2 1/2 inches at the top of the first page and 1/2 inch elsewhere, with black type of at least 10 point on white paper.
  • A foreign-language document comes with a written English translation.

The county notes that Public Acts 191 through 200 of 2018 changed some of these rules, and it points readers to the legislature's site to view the changes.

sections.h2: How much is Michigan transfer tax on an Isabella County sale?
sections.html:
Michigan taxes the transfer of real estate at the state level under Act 330 of 1993 and at the county level under Act 134 of 1966. Ask the Register of Deeds for the dollar amount at your sale price, and expect your title company to print it on the settlement statement.

A few statutory exemptions come up with house transfers, and both acts require the claim to appear on the deed:

  • A conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spouses.
  • A deed used to straighten a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • An instrument that confirms a title already vested, such as a quitclaim that fixes a flaw.
  • A joint tenancy created among people when at least one already owns the property.

Transfers to a child or grandchild appear only in the state act, which matters if you plan to gift a house to family.

sections.h2: Does a university town change how a house sale works?
sections.html:
The deed work does not change, but the market does. Central Michigan University is based in the county, and the Census Bureau lists a median age of 31.7 at the 2020 count, far below the other three counties in this set. QuickFacts shows 61.8 percent of housing owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024, the lowest share of the four, and the 2020 census put renters at 39.9 percent of occupied homes.

For a landlord selling a rental near campus, that means a deed from an investor-owned property that may have tenants in place. Check any lease before you set a closing date. Part of Mount Pleasant also lies within the Isabella Indian Reservation, which spans 217.67 square miles and is the main land base of the Saginaw Chippewa Tribal Nation. Ask your title company whether your parcel sits inside the reservation and what that means for the paperwork.

sections.h2: What do Isabella County housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
QuickFacts reports 64,691 people in July 2025, up 0.5 percent from the 2020 base. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $170,400 and median gross rent is $913. Median household income is $55,237, and 19.0 percent of residents are below the poverty line. A bachelor's degree or higher is held by 31.3 percent of adults, the highest rate of the four counties, and the average commute is 19.6 minutes.

The county issued 90 building permits in 2025. About 78.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which is lower than in the other three counties in this set.

sections.h2: How is the next tax bill affected after an Isabella County sale?
sections.html:
Michigan Treasury explains that a transfer of ownership uncaps the taxable value in the calendar year after the transfer, under Proposal A. The treasury site lists the Property Transfer Affidavit (Form 2766), which goes to the local assessor. Section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act lists transfers that do not uncap.

Tax assessment in Michigan is mostly a city and township task, not a county one. Contact the assessor for the city or township where the house sits about its taxable value and the filing deadline.

faqs.q: What does Isabella County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30.00 flat per document, plus $3.00 for each additional liber and page listed beyond the one included at no charge. A tax certificate, when required, costs $5.00 for up to five descriptions.

faqs.q: Who issues the tax certificate for an Isabella County warranty deed?
faqs.a: The Isabella County Treasurer. Your check for the certificate is payable to the Treasurer, and it must be obtained before the Register of Deeds records a warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed.

faqs.q: How do I get my recorded deed back from Isabella County?
faqs.a: Enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope with a mailed document. The office asks for one for return of mailed documents after recording.

faqs.q: Can the Isabella County Register of Deeds check my document for legal problems?
faqs.a: No. The office does not prepare documents or answer legal questions, and it recommends reviewing every document against the recording requirements before submitting it. Use an attorney for legal help.

faqs.q: What does a name search cost at the Isabella County office?
faqs.a: The charge is 50 cents for each year searched under MCL 600.2567, with a $5.00 minimum. Any copies you request from a search are billed at the statutory copy fee.
